solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree so great shelters the old woman

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: such means so great, as in 'such a fuss'
MA is an informal word for one's mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: A huge tree gives cover to an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumach is a shrub or small tree grown for its red autumn leaves and fruit, also spelt sumac.

clue.text: Highlight what PA would ask boss to do before email?

parts.words: what PA would ask boss to do
parts.note: a personal assistant brings letters for the boss to sign
post, or snail mail, came before email

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what an assistant needs from the boss before sending messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To signpost a point is to highlight or flag it clearly.

clue.text: This writer leads the way, penning good collection

indicators.note: leads means comes in front, so this word starts the answer

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as this writer, so ME

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one letter sits inside

parts.note: a lane is a way or path

explanation.surface: An author shows the way by putting together a fine anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, matching 'This writer', but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or assortment, a collection of varied things.

clue.text: Second race, with number two going badly as the roar goes up?

indicators.note: badly means in a mangled way, so these letters are jumbled
number two means the second letter of the word, which is taken away

explanation.surface: In a second race the runner-up falters while the crowd noise swells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with number two going' drops the A from RACE to leave RCE; 'badly' rearranges SECOND plus RCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a steady build in loudness, as when a crowd's noise swells.

clue.text: One coming in to cite holy writ, the result of division

indicators.note: something coming in enters another word, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: to quote is to cite
I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament, part of holy writ

explanation.surface: Someone quoting scripture reaches a conclusion, the answer to a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, dividing one number by another gives the quotient.

clue.text: Hundreds in Europe sadly having no exercise and lacking good food

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so these letters are scrambled
having no says the letters for exercise are taken out of the mix

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Masses across the continent, unhappily inactive and poorly fed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P and E from HUNDREDSINEUROPE and 'sadly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Undernourished means not getting enough healthy food to stay well.

clue.text: Out putting label on ducks

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this comes first

parts.note: a tab is a small label
O is a duck, a zero score in cricket, so two ducks are OO

explanation.surface: Someone sticking tags on waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' means not acceptable, as in 'that sort of talk is out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden or socially unacceptable, ruled out.

clue.text: Bringer of law, measure that performer must follow

indicators.note: must follow places this word after the one before it

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A legislator's bill must be followed by an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactor is one who enacts, making a measure into law.

clue.text: One band or another being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is spoken, so we want its sound

parts.note: another band here is a troop, a group of soldiers or scouts

explanation.surface: Choosing between two musical groups by listening to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of performers, a band of entertainers.

clue.text: See nerd undergo big change in place fostering new ideas?

indicators.note: a big change transforms the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Watch a geek go through a major transformation in an innovative setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding ground is figuratively a setting where ideas develop and multiply.

clue.text: Two sides bordering study covered in pleasant flowering plant

indicators.note: a thing covered in another sits inside it, so this group goes within the outer word

parts.note: good means pleasant, as in a good time

indicators.note: the two sides form a border on either side of the study, enclosing it

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two sides
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A study on the edge of a garden is draped in a lovely blooming plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a plant with tall spikes of small yellow flowers.

clue.text: Exist as a dissenter in the party

parts.note: to be is to exist
a 'no' is a vote against, so a dissenter

explanation.surface: Being the odd one out who disagrees at a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is an informal British word for a lively celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Face a revolutionary's self-assurance

parts.note: pan is slang for a face, as in deadpan
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: Confronting a rebel's cool confidence head on.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is stylish flair and confidence in how one does things.

clue.text: Situation for highest-level worker?

parts.note: sounds like a top job in a firm, but read literally it is where someone working at the greatest height stands, on top of a building

explanation.surface: A question about the post a senior executive holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer or steeplejack works up on the very top of a building, the highest place on it.

clue.text: Polish novel given English translation finally

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A book from Poland arrives at last in an English version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the noun meaning shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen is a soft shine on a surface, the gloss that polishing gives.

clue.text: Metal objects in club with damage through use reportedly

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the next part is what a word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: wear is damage caused by use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: A golf club worn down by heavy use, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironware is goods made of iron, such as pots, tools and fittings.

clue.text: Forest's team in domestic fixture

parts.note: a forest is a wood, and the 's adds S
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: Nottingham Forest's side playing a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest' and 'domestic fixture' suggest football, Nottingham Forest being an English club; a fixture is also a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood screw is a fixing used around the house, a fixture in the hardware sense.

clue.text: Running behind time, heading off with great excitement

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: belatedly means late, running behind time

explanation.surface: Late for an appointment, setting off in a thrilled rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Elatedly means in a joyful, excited manner.

clue.text: Gent, sorry when falling short, working to be sturdier

indicators.note: working means put to work, so the letters are reworked into a new order
falling short means the word stops before its end, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A gentleman, apologising for not measuring up, trains to get tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts SORRY to SORR; 'working' rearranges GENT plus SORR.
explanation.definitionFit: Stronger means more robust, the comparative of strong, as sturdier is of sturdy.

clue.text: For prominent one on board, tribute entertaining political leader

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding a guest within

parts.note: a toast is a tribute raised in drinks
PM is the prime minister

explanation.surface: A tribute to a senior figure on the board, with the prime minister as guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a company board; it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper mast on a sailing ship, standing high above the deck.

clue.text: Old king left some of the food offered by butcher?

definitions.text: some of the food offered by butcher?

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch abandoned a portion of meat from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an Anglo-Saxon king of Mercia in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the organ meat such as liver and kidneys that a butcher sells.

clue.text: Soldiers shut up in the bog get spruced up?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a fen is a bog or marsh
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
sh is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Troops confined to the latrine want a wash and brush-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' is British slang for a toilet, but here it is a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To freshen, or freshen up, is to tidy oneself and look smarter.

clue.text: County workers in a number of offices?

definitions.meaning: The usual abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county

definitions.text: workers in a number of offices?
definitions.meaning: the bodies of employees in several workplaces

explanation.definitionFit: Staffs abbreviates Staffordshire in the English Midlands, and staffs are groups of employees.

clue.text: Truck carrying litres for one who likes a drink or two?

definitions.text: one who likes a drink or two?

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a tipper is a truck whose load tips out

explanation.surface: A lorry hauling litres of liquid for someone fond of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker of alcohol.

clue.text: Place offering food for preacher John — without end

indicators.note: without end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: John the Baptist lived on locusts and wild honey in the desert

explanation.surface: A spot to feed a preacher endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a particular position or site, Latin for place.

clue.text: Dodgy cult with unique feature for those buying into it

indicators.note: one part goes into the other, the 'it' being the cult

parts.note: a sect is a cult or religious group
USP is the unique selling point, a feature that attracts buyers

explanation.surface: A shady cult offers a special selling point to the gullible who sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buying into it' looks like part of the cult story; 'into it' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect describes something that cannot be trusted, just as dodgy does informally.

clue.text: Football club has managed to save money in Switzerland?

indicators.note: to save is to keep in hand, so the club holds the next word inside

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A football club has pulled off saving money in a Swiss bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc is the currency of Switzerland.

clue.text: Discovered part of Peru near the desert

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something found in a region of Peru close to the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthed means dug up, hence found or brought to light.

clue.text: Time in coastal location where wild flowers can prosper?

indicators.note: in says this letter sits inside the place that follows

parts.note: the seaside is a coastal location

explanation.surface: A spell at the coast where wild flowers flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Set-aside is farmland deliberately left uncultivated, under an EU scheme, so wild plants grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-aside land is taken out of crop production and left to nature, letting wild flowers thrive.

clue.text: Number bunked off in gutless endeavour

indicators.note: in says this word goes inside the trimmed one
gutless means without its insides, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: a try is an endeavour or attempt
went means left, as when someone bunked off

explanation.surface: A total of truants skipped out on a feeble effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a number, two tens.
